newsitem.title: ISRAEL: FDA clears ESC laser for sale in U.S..
newsitem.headline: FDA clears ESC laser for sale in U.S..

text.p: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has given clearance for Israel's ESC Medical Systems Ltd to market its Topaz 30 surgical CO2 laser system in the United States, ESC said on Tuesday.

The system is used for general surgical and dermatological applications, including fast growing skin resurfacing work. ESC, a maker of cosmetic surgery lasers, said there were already 60 systems sold and placed outside the United States.

"Looking ahead, we are awaiting FDA marketing clearance for our more advanced skin resurfacing laser, the Derma 20 as well as our Epilight hair removal system," Shimon Eckhouse, president and chief executive officer of ESC, said in a statement.
Earlier this month, ESC said it had completed acquisition of U.S.-based Luxar Corp, a designer and manufacturer of surgical cosmetic lasers and related products.
Luxar brought to the deal an installed based in the United States of over 3,000 lasers, a 65-strong U.S. sales force and international distributors.
ESC, whose first product was launched in 1995, has only 15 salespeople and an installed base of 400 units.

Luxar, founded in 1988, had net sales of $28.1 million in the year ended September 30, 1996, close to ESC's $32.9 million for calendar 1996. But Luxar reported net earnings of just $4.5 million against ESC's $12.7 million.
